rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results <U+2014> Cosmos probe installed at CER experimental farm near Mezzolara di Budrio (Po valley, Italy) with hourly neutron counts over the 2014<U+2013>2015 seasons, compared with the authors' own soil cores, profile probes (12 access tubes, 25<U+2013>100 m) and buried sensors (Table IV, Figures 7<U+2013>17).
rows.notes: The study is a primary field verification of the Cosmos (CRNS) probe's measurement accuracy, effective depth and horizontal footprint. It shows Cosmos soil moisture agrees with cores, profile probes and sensors for the top 0<U+2013>50/60 cm (RMSE 0.029<U+2013>0.067, overall 0.039) and at least 100 m horizontally, and derives a colour-coded soil moisture deficit (Figures 2b, 18) that it says 'could be made operational' for deciding when and how much to irrigate. It does not implement Cosmos-based irrigation scheduling, nor measure applied water, water savings, yield or water-use efficiency; the scheduling/WUE benefit is only proposed in the Discussion and Conclusion. This is a precondition (accurate area-based soil moisture/SMD monitoring) of the claimed water-conservation effect, so Q2 is no and upstream is true. The RMSE values and the stated limitations (no access tubes beyond 100 m, biomass correction via modelled dry matter, hypothetical depth equation) concern measurement accuracy, not the claimed effect, so Q8/Q9 remain no.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study concerns CRNS/Cosmos soil moisture measurement validation at one Italian site over two seasons; irrigation scheduling and water-use efficiency outcomes are proposed, not tested.
